parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: Storm Night
parts.body: What did the storm change in Palmetto Springs, and was all of it bad?

welcome.script:
(Hold up a flashlight and a bottle of water.) If a hurricane were coming tonight, what would you grab first?

[ON SCREEN: The town map]
A hurricane is heading for Palmetto Springs, June’s town. Look at the red zone by the bay. Those families have to leave before the storm.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
Tonight you’ll stay up with June, hour by hour. In the morning, you’ll figure out what the storm changed, and whether all of it was bad. Press Listen to hear from June, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · the weather radio (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Make an alarm sound: beep, beep, beep!) That’s what a weather radio sounds like. It wakes up when dangerous weather is coming.

[ON SCREEN: The weather radio]
Press Play and listen to the warning. Then tap the three dangers the storm is bringing. Careful: a place or a time is not a danger.

Then write three things the storm might change in town. Think beyond buildings! Press Listen for June’s tip.

part1.script:
(Push one domino with your finger, or tap one block into another.) A cause makes something happen. The effect is what changes.

[ON SCREEN: The storm clock]
Press the button to move through the night. When a call comes in, drag the danger that caused it onto the call.

[ON SCREEN: The tide gauge]
Keep your eye on the tide gauge. Normal high tide is about two feet. What happens at midnight? Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · trace the chain (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🔗 Trace the chain
parts.title: Cause → Land → Ecosystem → People
parts.body: Follow the storm surge. Two cards come from a different danger.

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: The morning after]
This is a real Florida town the morning after Hurricane Michael. You stamped what changed: the land, the ecosystem and the people.

[ON SCREEN: Trace the chain]
Now let’s link it all together, like dominoes. Follow the storm surge: the cause, then the land, the ecosystem and the people. Two cards don’t belong. Then press June’s last reading. I think it will surprise you! Press Listen.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab: what did the storm change, and was all of it bad?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, a cause-and-effect chain for any Florida natural event in Part C, and a CER. Want to sketch your chain? That’s a bonus. Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “All natural events are disasters. The fewer of them we have, the better.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says all natural events are disasters. Hmm. Think about Bay Street. Now think about June’s spring.

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Remember CER. Tap your side and two facts from today. Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.script:
Case closed! You stayed up all night with June, and you traced one storm through the land, the ecosystem and the people. You even found the good side.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and the tide gauge chart goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Remember the houses still standing in Mexico Beach? Next time, we think like engineers: how can a town stay safer in the next storm? Press Listen for June’s last word.

part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: Before]
This is Mexico Beach, a real Florida town, before Hurricane Michael.

[ON SCREEN: After]
And this is the same spot the next day. Drag the slider, tap each number and stamp it: land, ecosystem or people. Press Listen.

quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
